newsitem.title: USA: San Onofre 1,070 MW nuke seen up Tues afternoon.
newsitem.headline: San Onofre 1,070 MW nuke seen up Tues afternoon.

text.p: The 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant in San Clemente, Calif., is expected to synchronize with the regional power grid sometime late Tuesday afternoon, a spokesman for the plant said Monday.
The unit, which was shut June 29 to replace check valves, is then expected to take between 24 and 72 hours to ascend to full power, the spokesman added.
Meanwhile, San Onofre's 1,080 MW unit 3 is still scheduled to restart on Thursday.
Unit 3 has been off line since April 12 for a scheduled refueling outage, which was extended for additional work.
The San Onofre plant is 75 percent owned by Southern California Edison Co, which also operates the plant.
